Report_ID: Hematoma expansion (>6-mL absolute increase in hematoma volume) on 24-h CT
Title: Tranexamic Acid for Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Randomized Controlled Pilot Trial (ISRCTN50867461)
Author: Sprigg, Renton, Dineen, Kwong, Bath
Comment: Denominators used are the numbers randomised (ITT: 16 TA, 8 placebo). The table's '24 h CT, patients' row lists 16 TA and 7 placebo (one placebo patient had no 24-h CT), but the reported placebo percentage (12.5% = 1/8) is based on the randomised denominator of 8. The paper names no effect measure (comparison by Fisher exact/chi-square, 2P = 1.00).; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Tranexamic acid (IV 1 g bolus over 10 min + 1 g infusion over 8 h)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Design Type: randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, blinded-endpoint pilot trial (2:1 allocation)

Recruitment source: Stroke service, Nottingham University Hospital NHS Trust
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of participants with >6 mL absolute increase in hematoma volume between baseline and 24-h CT

Report_ID: Number of participants with haematoma expansion at 24 hours (any increase in volume on 24-h CT)
Title: Tranexamic Acid as Antifibrinolytic Agent in Non Traumatic Intracerebral Hemorrhages
Author: Arumugam et al.
Comment: The trial does not state a conventional dichotomous definition of expansion (e.g. >=33% or >=6 mL). Treatment events (11/15) are stated verbatim in the Result section; control events (15/15) are derived by counting the 15 positive volume differences listed for the control group in Table 2 (all patients expanded, +0.74 to +13.79 cm3). ITT denominator = 15 randomised per arm. If the >=6 mL definition were used instead, counts would be 0/15 (TXA) vs 3/15 (control) - patient nos. 6, 14, 15 expanded 6.32-13.79 cm3. Table 4 lists treatment patient 14 as -0.55 while Table 3 lists +0.55 (inconsistency); the Result-section count of 11 expanders was retained.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Tranexamic acid 1 g IV bolus + 1 g/h infusion for 8 h, plus strict BP control') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); unsupported or insufficient statistic type
Participant type: Adults (>=18 y) with acute (<8 h) spontaneous hypertensive supratentorial intracerebral haemorrhage, non-surgically managed
Recruitment source: Emergency department / Department of Neurosurgery, Hospital Sultanah Aminah Johor
Outcome measurement: Count of patients with a positive change in haematoma volume between the 1st and 2nd (24-hour) CT brain scan, out of 15 randomised per arm
Outcome variable: Number of participants with haematoma expansion at 24 hours (any increase in volume on 24-h CT)

Author: Sprigg N, et al. (TICH-2 Investigators)
Comment: Per the synthesis plan, totals are the numbers RANDOMISED to each arm (ITT denominators: 1161 tranexamic acid, 1164 placebo); the paper's own percentages (25% and 29%) are calculated on the smaller numbers with a 24 h scan (1054 and 1058), which are recorded in group_1_n/group_2_n. Report_ID: Haematoma expansion at 24 hours (absolute increase >6 mL or relative growth >33% from baseline)
Title: Tranexamic acid for acute intracerebral haemorrhage growth based on imaging assessment (TRAIGE): a multicentre, randomised, placebo-controlled trial
Author: Liu J, Nie X, Gu H, et al.
Comment: Paper reports an odds ratio (binary logistic regression), not a risk ratio; RR to be computed downstream from the extracted event counts. Denominators used are the numbers randomised (89 TXA, 82 placebo); 2 TXA patients with missing 24-hour imaging were imputed as having growth (worst case), consistent with ITT. Component rows in Table 3 (ICH growth volume >6 mL: 26/89 vs 28/82, OR 0.80 (0.42-1.52), p=0.49; ICH growth rate >33%: 23/89 vs 25/82, OR 0.80 (0.41-1.55), p=0.50) not recorded separately to avoid double counting the same construct.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Tranexamic acid (1 g IV over 10 min then 1 g over 8 hours)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: Adults (18-79 y) with acute primary spontaneous supratentorial intracerebral haemorrhage and imaging markers of expansion (spot, black hole or blend sign), treated within 8 h of onset
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of participants with intracerebral haematoma growth at 24 hours, ITT denominators (89 TXA, 82 placebo; 2 missing 24-hour scans imputed as worst case = growth)
Outcome variable: Haematoma expansion at 24 hours (absolute increase >6 mL or relative growth >33% from baseline)
